rules.instruction: Inspect all specified source systems, identify the authoritative roster and relevant status/submission fields, and reconcile records using stable identifiers rather than names alone. Exclude entities explicitly marked inactive, withdrawn, or otherwise out of scope before determining missing items. Report the complete in-scope population, matched submissions, missing entities, and the contact data needed for downstream action, preserving names and identifiers exactly as supported by the sources.
rules.trigger_description: When a task requires identifying missing submissions or other participant-level actions by reconciling an email source with a structured course or organizational roster.
required_evidence: Source names or descriptions and why each is authoritative
Roster status evidence supporting inclusion or exclusion
Submission evidence for each matched record or a documented complete search basis
Stable ID, name, and contact mapping for every downstream recipient
Counts that reconcile across total, excluded, matched, and missing populations
rules.verification: Independently recompute the reconciliation from the source data, check for duplicate IDs, name/ID mismatches, omitted records, and excluded-status violations; confirm that reported counts and recipient list agree with the evidence.
rules.fallback: If sources conflict or a record cannot be matched confidently, flag it with the competing evidence and uncertainty instead of guessing; provide a conservative list of confirmed records and state what additional confirmation is needed.
rules.context_notes: The observed trace used this inspection/reconciliation handoff successfully; the downstream execution achieved full recipient coverage with no duplicates or omissions and passed independent verification. The contract generalizes that evidence-first reconciliation pattern without depending on task-specific file or course details.

rules.instruction: Independently recompute the in-scope roster and missing-submission set from the authoritative structured records and message sources, excluding withdrawn or otherwise out-of-scope participants. Verify each approved email one-for-one by stable participant ID, recipient address, subject, and body fields required to identify the participant, then read back sent-message state and reconcile prior plus newly sent messages against the expected set. Report exact counts and any duplicate, omission, extra, failed, or unverifiable records; approve completion only when every expected recipient has recipient-level evidence.
rules.trigger_description: When a reconciled roster is used to send individualized submission reminders to participants who are missing a required item, and completion must be confirmed at recipient level.
required_evidence: Authoritative roster and submission-status search basis
Explicit withdrawal or out-of-scope evidence for exclusions
Stable participant ID, name, and recipient mapping for every expected reminder
Per-message recipient-level readback with subject and required identity fields checked
Reconciled expected versus sent counts and explicit duplicate, omission, extra, failure, and uncertainty report
rules.verification: Independently recompute the eligible missing-submission population, compare every sent message to the expected manifest by stable ID and recipient, validate the required subject and body identity fields, and approve only exact one-to-one coverage with no unresolved remainder.
rules.fallback: If roster, submission, contact, message readback, or exclusion evidence is incomplete, separate confirmed from unverified recipients, list the exact remaining IDs and evidence gaps, and keep the completion decision closed rather than inferring delivery from aggregate counts.

rules.instruction: Accept only a complete approved reminder manifest from the planner. For each item, preserve the source-backed title, reminder-start time, deadline/end time, timezone, description, and any required link or location; treat the reminder as a deadline action rather than requiring meeting evidence. Validate the native calendar contract and all item payloads before mutation, then create every feasible item, recording durable per-item outcomes. Read back the provider state and reconcile pre-existing plus newly created entries one-for-one with the approved set, checking duplicates, omissions, extras, timing, timezone, descriptions, and reminder behavior. Keep completion closed and report the exact remaining or failed items if execution is interrupted or incomplete.
rules.trigger_description: When a planner has reconciled multiple source-backed deadline or explicitly requested reminder items and the implementer must create corresponding calendar entries without confusing them with meetings.
required_evidence: Planner-confirmed complete expected set with stable source identifiers
Source-backed reminder and deadline/end times, timezone, title, description, and requested reminder behavior for every item
Explicit excluded or unresolved candidates with evidence gaps
Validation of the calendar interface/contract before mutation
Provider readback distinguishing pre-existing, newly created, failed, and remaining items
One-to-one reconciliation of expected versus actual entries with duplicate, omission, extra, and field checks
rules.verification: Independently compare each read-back calendar entry with its approved source specification; verify the deadline-reminder classification, title, times, timezone, description, and reminder settings, and confirm that all approved items are covered exactly once with no deadline-derived extras.
rules.fallback: If the approved set, source fields, interface contract, or provider readback is incomplete, pause affected mutations and return the evidence gaps. If execution is partial or interrupted, preserve successful entries, report completed, failed, and remaining identifiers, keep the completion gate closed, and provide a resumable continuation set rather than claiming completion.
rules.context_notes: This task passed after all required calendar entries were created and independently read back, with consistent reminder-start/deadline timing, timezone, title, and required description across the complete multi-item set. The new contract complements the existing meeting-specific rule by covering explicit deadline reminders, which must not be forced through meeting classification.

rules.instruction: Inspect all relevant workspace and email sources before calendar mutation. Enumerate the complete set of requested deadline or reminder items, distinguish explicit deadlines from meetings and unrelated dates, reconcile duplicate or updated records using source authority and chronology, and extract source-backed title, deadline/start and end times, timezone, location or link when present, reminder offset, and required description. Return included items plus excluded or unresolved candidates with evidence so downstream execution can act on the complete approved set and preserve uncertainty.
rules.trigger_description: When a task requires finding multiple source-backed deadlines or explicitly requested reminder items across email or workspace materials and translating them into a complete calendar-ready set before mutation.
required_evidence: Complete search basis for relevant workspace and email sources
Per-item evidence that the requested action is a deadline reminder or other explicitly actionable calendar item
Exact source-backed title, date/time, timezone, reminder offset, and required description for every included item
Provenance and conflict-resolution evidence for duplicates or updated source records
Explicit excluded and unresolved candidates with reasons
Reconciled candidate and included-item counts with duplicate and omission checks
rules.verification: Independently compare the returned set against the authoritative sources; verify every included item exactly once, confirm deadline-versus-meeting classification, timing, timezone, reminder offset, title, and required description, and check that excluded or unresolved candidates are not silently scheduled.
rules.fallback: If source coverage, deadline timing, timezone, reminder offset, or event requirements are ambiguous or conflicting, return the affected items as unresolved with provenance and schedule only confidently supported reminders; do not infer missing times or silently merge duplicates.
rules.context_notes: The current run passed after a generic planner-to-context-analyst request to inspect workspace files and enumerate all email/calendar requirements; the resulting set covered all required calendar items and was independently read back. Existing meeting-specific guidance remains useful for true meetings, but this separate contract covers source-backed deadline reminders without conflating them with meeting events.

rules.instruction: Before mutating the calendar, require a calendar-ready specification for each item that explicitly establishes that it is a meeting, not merely a deadline, conference submission date, or other date. Use only source-backed title, start time, timezone, location or link, and requested reminder offset. Do not infer a meeting from a deadline or create an event for every similarly named item. If the source contains only deadlines or lacks an explicit meeting time, pause and return those items as unresolved rather than scheduling them. After creation, read back the events and reconcile them one-for-one with the approved meeting set, recording any pre-existing, newly created, failed, duplicate, or extra events.
rules.trigger_description: When an implementer is asked to create calendar reminders from email or workspace information and must act only after the intended meetings and reminder timing have been identified.
required_evidence: Explicit source evidence that every scheduled item is a meeting and not only a deadline or submission date
Exact source-backed start time, timezone, title, and reminder offset for each item
Provenance and uncertainty for conflicting, duplicate, or updated source records
An explicit excluded/unresolved list for candidates lacking meeting evidence or timing
Calendar/provider readback and one-to-one reconciliation against the approved meeting set
rules.verification: Independently compare each created event with its source evidence and approved specification; verify meeting status, title, start time, timezone, reminder offset, and location/link, then confirm there are no omissions, duplicates, or extra deadline-derived events.
rules.fallback: If the source material supplies only deadlines, ambiguous dates, inaccessible records, or conflicting meeting details, do not mutate the calendar for those items. Return the evidence gap and schedule only confidently supported meetings; if none are supported, report that no calendar action is justified.

rules.instruction: Use only the approved source-reconciled assignment and quiz manifest. Preserve both existing filenames and headers exactly, write assignments and quizzes to their designated CSV files, retain source-backed field values, and order each file by deadline ascending with class-code dictionary ordering for equal deadlines. Validate the manifest and CSV format before writing, then read both files back and reconcile rows one-for-one against the expected set, checking duplicates, omissions, extras, key uniqueness, headers, byte/format consistency, and ordering. Report any unresolved or unverifiable records separately and do not claim completion if coverage is partial.
rules.trigger_description: When a planner has identified a complete, ordered set of unfinished course assignments and quizzes and the implementer must populate existing CSV artifacts without renaming them or changing their schema.

artifact_requirements.ordering_rule: deadline ascending; class code dictionary order for ties

required_evidence: Complete approved manifest with stable course and activity identifiers
Explicit exclusions or unresolved activities with evidence
Verbatim target headers and filename-preservation requirements
Per-row source provenance and ordering keys
Readback of both CSV files with row counts, key-set reconciliation, duplicate/omission/extra checks, and ordering validation
rules.fallback: If the manifest, schema, source fields, or file readback is incomplete or conflicting, pause affected writes and return the evidence gap. Preserve successfully written rows, list exact missing or unverifiable activity IDs, and keep completion unconfirmed until a resumable set can be reconciled.
rules.context_notes: Retain the active canvas_unfinished_work_reconciliation rule for source analysis; this rule covers downstream artifact writing and verification only.

rules.instruction: Recompute the expected unfinished assignment and quiz population from authoritative course-platform records, teacher announcements, and submission status using stable course and activity identifiers. Independently compare both final CSVs cell-by-cell with that expected manifest; confirm submitted and explicitly non-submission activities are absent, headers and filenames are unchanged, assignment/quiz placement is correct, deadlines sort ascending with class-code dictionary tie-breaking, and there are no duplicate, missing, extra, or unresolved rows. Report separate assignment and quiz counts plus any evidence gaps; approve completion only when both files reconcile exactly.
rules.trigger_description: When a student's unfinished assignments and quizzes have been written to existing CSV artifacts and an independent verifier must confirm source completeness, exclusions, schema fidelity, and ordering before completion is reported.
required_evidence: Complete search basis for authoritative course records, announcements, activity definitions, and submission status
Stable course and activity identifiers with inclusion or exclusion evidence
Verbatim CSV headers and filename-preservation/readback evidence
Cell-level comparison of every expected row and every actual row
Separate counts and checks for assignment and quiz files, including deadline and tie-break ordering
Explicit duplicate, omission, extra, and unresolved-record report
rules.verification: Independently recompute the source population and compare expected and actual key sets and field values one-for-one for each CSV; verify headers, filenames, row counts, deduplication, exclusions, deadline parsing, and class-code tie ordering. Completion is approved only if both files have exact coverage and no unresolved or unverifiable rows.
rules.fallback: If source records, announcement evidence, submission status, CSV readback, or a field comparison is incomplete, report confirmed versus unverified coverage separately and list exact affected activity IDs. Do not infer missing values or treat a structurally valid artifact, manifest, or partial readback as proof of completion.
rules.context_notes: Retains the existing source-reconciliation and artifact-execution guidance while adding the missing receiver-specific independent verification contract; no provider or API failure is implicated.

rules.instruction: Review the approved assignment and quiz manifest, native contract, workspace file requirements, and post-write readback as separate evidence. Confirm both existing filenames and headers are preserved, rows are in the designated files, source-backed fields and ordering are unchanged, and expected versus actual stable activity keys reconcile one-for-one with no duplicates, omissions, extras, or unresolved records. Reconcile source coverage, manifest counts, artifact counts, and verifier findings; report go/no-go and keep completion unconfirmed for any mismatch or missing readback.
rules.trigger_description: When a student's source-reconciled unfinished assignments and quizzes are written to existing CSV artifacts and an integrator must coordinate final readiness and cross-artifact completeness checks before completion is reported.
required_evidence: Planner-approved source manifest with stable course and activity identifiers and explicit exclusions or unresolved items
Native contract and workspace requirements, including exact filenames, headers, and assignment/quiz file mapping
Independent readback of both CSVs with row counts and stable-key reconciliation
Evidence that source-backed fields, deadline ordering, and class-code tie ordering are preserved
Explicit duplicate, omission, extra, unresolved, and remaining-record checks
Separate assignment and quiz counts that reconcile across source manifest and artifacts
rules.verification: Compare the union of actual rows in both CSVs with the approved manifest separately by file; verify filenames, headers, cell values, deduplication, exclusions, deadline sorting, and class-code tie-breaking. Do not treat a structurally valid file or ready contract as proof of source completeness without the independent source and readback comparisons.
rules.fallback: If the manifest, native contract, source coverage, or file readback is incomplete or conflicting, return the exact evidence gaps and affected activity IDs. Preserve confirmed artifact state, keep the go/no-go decision closed, and provide a resumable reconciliation set rather than inferring values or claiming completion.
rules.context_notes: The contract is deliberately about information integrity and go/no-go reporting, not file-editing mechanics; the implementer and verifier remain responsible for their respective execution and independent source checks.

rules.instruction: Inspect the authoritative course-platform records, teacher announcements, assignment/quiz definitions, submission status, and the target CSV schema before any edits. Reconcile courses and activities using stable course and activity identifiers; include only items that are unfinished for the student and that the source evidence shows must be submitted. Exclude submitted items, explicitly non-submission content, closed or otherwise out-of-scope items, and duplicates. Preserve exact source-backed titles, class codes, deadlines, and required CSV fields, documenting uncertainty rather than guessing. Return a complete manifest, explicit exclusions/unresolved items, and the ordering key: deadline ascending, then class code dictionary order for equal deadlines.
rules.trigger_description: When a task requires identifying a student's incomplete, still-submittable assignments or quizzes from course-platform data, announcements, and submission records, then preparing a complete ordered set for spreadsheet entry.
required_evidence: Complete search basis for authoritative course data, announcements, activity definitions, and student submission status
Stable course/activity identifiers and explicit inclusion or exclusion evidence for every reviewed activity
Announcement or equivalent teacher-source evidence when determining that content must or need not be submitted
Submission-status evidence for each included or excluded activity
Verbatim target CSV headers and evidence that the proposed values conform to existing examples
Per-field provenance, uncertainty, and justification for any TBD value
Reconciled counts and duplicate/omission checks across the full reviewed population
Explicit ordering keys showing deadline ascending and class-code tie-breaking
rules.verification: Independently recompute the in-scope activity population from the authoritative platform data, compare submission and teacher-announcement evidence for every activity, verify that submitted or explicitly non-submission items are absent, and reconcile the included assignment and quiz manifests one-for-one against the source population. Check headers, field values, deadline parsing, tie-break ordering, duplicates, omissions, and unresolved records.
rules.fallback: If course access, announcement evidence, activity identity, deadline, submission status, or CSV schema is incomplete or conflicting, do not infer inclusion or values. Return the affected records as unresolved with competing evidence, provide only confidently supported rows, and state what confirmation is needed before downstream editing.
rules.context_notes: This contract is supported by the successful run in which local authoritative Canvas data, announcements, activity definitions, and submission status yielded 65/65 verified rows (22 assignments and 43 quizzes), with submitted assignments excluded, zero duplicates or extras, unchanged headers, and correct deadline/class-code ordering. It adds the missing explicit evidence and payload structure to the previously generic context-analysis handoff without attributing unrelated provider/login limitations to the collaboration protocol.

rules.instruction: Before any external or irreversible action, inspect the available interfaces and authoritative inputs, then stage the individualized payloads and an execution manifest. Use only the source-reconciled expected set and source-backed identifiers, preserving exclusions and existing-completion evidence. Validate each payload and the required interface contract before the send/write gate. Execute in bounded batches with durable per-record checkpoints; after every batch, read back the provider state and update the manifest so a later continuation can resume from the exact remaining set without duplicating successful actions. Do not stop after a canary or partial batch unless the interface, time, or provider genuinely prevents continuation; if interrupted, explicitly report the completed, attempted, remaining, and failed records and leave the task gate closed. After all feasible batches, reconcile the union of pre-existing and newly successful records one-for-one against the approved expected set, with provider/readback evidence and duplicate, omission, extra, and failure checks. Never claim completion when the expected set is only partially covered.
rules.trigger_description: When a planner has a source-reconciled set of records and the implementer must perform many individualized external actions, possibly across a spreadsheet and notifications, including work already completed or executed in batches.
required_evidence: Upstream-confirmed expected set with stable identifiers and exclusion status
Evidence for every action already completed and an explicit remaining set
Per-record payload and artifact/interface validation before mutation
Durable batch checkpoints and provider readback sufficient to resume without resending successes
Provider/readback confirmation separating prior, newly successful, failed, and remaining records
Independent reconciliation of expected versus completed actions, including duplicate, omission, extra, and failure checks
An explicit closed completion gate whenever any approved record remains incomplete
rules.verification: Compare the union of previously completed and newly successful records with the planner-approved expected set; verify each record is covered exactly once, each payload contains the correct source-backed identifier and required content, each batch checkpoint agrees with provider readback, and counts reconcile across successful, failed, and remaining records. Confirm that partial execution is not represented as completion and that any continuation starts only from the recorded remaining set.
rules.fallback: If the expected set, prior-completion evidence, payloads, manifest, interface contract, checkpoints, or readback are not confirmed, pause mutation and return the unresolved records and evidence gaps. If execution is interrupted or a provider/interface limitation prevents completion, preserve successful records, report exact progress and remaining work, keep the completion gate closed, and provide a resumable continuation plan rather than claiming success.
rules.context_notes: The current run produced validated execution artifacts and honest partial counts, so the refinement focuses on resumability and completion accounting rather than adding unsupported source requirements or blaming an external provider.

version_history.instruction: Before performing any external or irreversible action, inspect the available interfaces and prepare the required execution artifacts. Use only the recipient list and individualized payloads supported by the upstream reconciliation, preserve source-backed names and stable identifiers, and wait until completeness and exclusions are confirmed. After execution, provide an auditable outcome and verification results, including counts, duplicate/omission checks, and confirmation that required artifacts were updated.
version_history.trigger_description: When a planner has obtained a source-reconciled list of in-scope recipients and the implementer must carry out external actions while producing required artifacts and verifiable completion evidence.
required_evidence: Upstream-confirmed recipient list with stable identifiers and exclusion status
Per-recipient payloads or a documented basis that each payload is correctly individualized
Evidence that required execution artifacts were prepared or updated
Provider/readback confirmation of attempted and successful actions
Independent reconciliation of expected versus completed actions, including duplicate and omission checks
version_history.verification: Compare the executed records with the planner-approved recipient set; verify each payload contains the correct source-backed identifier and required content, confirm provider or system readback, check for duplicates, omissions, and failures, and independently validate the recorded artifacts and counts.
version_history.fallback: If the recipient set, per-recipient payloads, or source-backed identifiers are not confirmed, pause external actions and return the unresolved records and evidence gaps to the planner for clarification. If an artifact or capability is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming completion.
version_history.context_notes: The observed planner-to-implementer handoff was followed by a successful execution and full verification. This complements the existing reconciliation rule by covering the transition from confirmed findings to external actions and required run artifacts.
version_history.reason: Retain the existing successful source-backed execution, artifact, readback, and completeness guidance. Refine it to make the observed partial execution explicit: the planner identified one already-sent canary and instructed the implementer to send only the remaining records, while the run still achieved full coverage with no duplicates or omissions. This adds a reusable prior-completion/remaining-set contract without introducing task-specific details or changing the other valid safeguards.

version_history.instruction: Before any external or irreversible action, inspect the available interfaces and prepare the required execution artifacts. Use only the source-reconciled recipient set and individualized payloads supported by upstream evidence. Reconcile the expected set against any already-completed actions before sending, treating prior successes as completed rather than resending them; preserve source-backed names and stable identifiers, and confirm exclusions and completeness. After execution, provide an auditable outcome distinguishing pre-existing, newly attempted, successful, and failed records, with provider/readback evidence and duplicate/omission checks.
version_history.trigger_description: When a planner has a source-reconciled set of in-scope recipients and the implementer must perform external actions, including cases where some actions were already completed or used as a canary.
required_evidence: Upstream-confirmed expected recipient set with stable identifiers and exclusion status
Evidence for every action already completed before the handoff and an explicit remaining set
Per-recipient payloads or a documented basis that each new payload is correctly individualized
Evidence that required execution artifacts were prepared or updated
Provider/readback confirmation separating prior and newly executed actions
Independent reconciliation of expected versus completed actions, including duplicate, omission, and failure checks
version_history.verification: Compare the union of previously completed and newly successful records with the planner-approved expected set; verify each record is covered exactly once, each new payload contains the correct source-backed identifier and required content, confirm provider or system readback, and validate recorded artifacts and counts.
version_history.fallback: If the expected set, prior-completion evidence, remaining records, or source-backed identifiers are not confirmed, pause external actions and return the unresolved records and evidence gaps to the planner. If an artifact, interface, or readback capability is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming completion.
version_history.context_notes: The current task passed evaluation with complete recipient coverage, no duplicates or omissions, MCP readback, independent verification, and required artifact updates. The refinement addresses the handoff trace's explicit distinction between an already completed action and the remaining actions.
version_history.reason: Refined the existing implementer contract rather than creating a duplicate rule. The current trace shows that successful execution depended on first inspecting the workspace and execution contract, preparing recipient-specific artifacts and a manifest, withholding sends during preparation, and only then executing and verifying all actions. The prior rule covered preparation generally but did not make the per-recipient artifact-content/format checks or explicit send gate sufficiently actionable; its valid reconciliation and readback guidance is preserved.

version_history.instruction: Before any external or irreversible action, inspect the available interfaces and authoritative inputs, then stage the required individualized artifacts and execution manifest. Use only the source-reconciled recipient set and individualized payloads supported by upstream evidence. Reconcile the expected set against any already-completed actions before sending, treating prior successes as completed rather than resending them; preserve source-backed names and stable identifiers, and confirm exclusions and completeness. Validate that each recipient's artifact contains the requested materials and required structure, naming, or format before the send gate. Do not send until the staged artifacts, manifest, recipient mapping, and required interface contract are readable and internally consistent. After execution, provide an auditable outcome distinguishing pre-existing, newly attempted, successful, and failed records, with provider/readback evidence and duplicate/omission checks.
version_history.trigger_description: When a planner has a source-reconciled set of in-scope recipients and the implementer must prepare individualized submission artifacts and perform external actions, including cases where some actions were already completed or used as a canary.
required_evidence: Upstream-confirmed expected recipient set with stable identifiers and exclusion status
Evidence for every action already completed before the handoff and an explicit remaining set
Per-recipient payloads and evidence that each staged artifact contains the requested source-backed materials in the required structure, naming, and format
Evidence that required execution artifacts, manifest, and interface contract were prepared, readable, and updated before sending
Provider/readback confirmation separating prior and newly executed actions
Independent reconciliation of expected versus completed actions, including duplicate, omission, and failure checks
version_history.verification: Compare the union of previously completed and newly successful records with the planner-approved expected set; verify each record is covered exactly once, each new payload contains the correct source-backed identifier and required content, each staged artifact passes its content/format check, confirm provider or system readback, and validate recorded artifacts, manifest, and counts.
version_history.fallback: If the expected set, prior-completion evidence, remaining records, source-backed identifiers, artifact contents, or manifest/interface contract are not confirmed, pause external actions and return the unresolved records and evidence gaps to the planner. If an artifact, interface, or readback capability is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming completion.
version_history.context_notes: Retained the existing source-reconciled execution, prior-versus-new distinction, exclusion checks, readback, and completeness reconciliation. Added a reusable pre-send staging gate for individualized submission artifacts and the execution manifest/interface contract because the current successful trace explicitly required preparing these artifacts before sends and then verified complete artifact and recipient coverage. No task-specific filenames or one-off details are encoded.
version_history.reason: Retain the existing source-reconciled recipient selection, individualized artifact validation, prior-versus-new distinction, readback, and completeness reconciliation. Add bounded batch checkpoints, resumable remaining-set handling, and an explicit closed completion gate because this trace achieved only 30 of 110 sheet records and 5 of 110 notifications; the outcome correctly exposed blockers, but future handoffs should make partial progress durable and prevent a canary or interrupted batch from being the terminal execution state. This addresses the handoff's completeness and continuation needs without treating the partial result as evidence of an API/provider failure.

rules.instruction: Inspect the current mailbox, workspace materials, and available memory context without sending or submitting anything. Identify every in-scope reply, determine whether it explicitly requires application-material submission, extract the exact recipient and requested contents/format, and map each requirement to source-backed workspace materials. Preserve uncertainty where a request, recipient, or material match is ambiguous, and return a complete actionable set for downstream preparation and verification.
rules.trigger_description: When a task requires finding actionable replies in an inbox and determining which requests require submission of materials before any external action is taken.
required_evidence: Mailbox search basis and evidence for complete coverage of relevant replies
Per-reply evidence that submission is required or not required
Exact recipient and requested materials/format extracted from the message
Source-backed mapping from each requested item to available workspace materials
Any memory-derived personal information used, with uncertainty noted
Counts reconciling reviewed, actionable, and non-actionable replies
rules.verification: Independently check the mailbox search coverage, confirm each actionable reply is included exactly once, verify recipient and requirement extraction against the original message, and confirm every requested material has either a source-backed workspace match or an explicit gap/uncertainty.
rules.fallback: If mailbox access, workspace materials, memory context, or a message-to-material match is incomplete, do not infer missing details; return the affected replies with the evidence gap and limit the actionable set to confidently supported records.

rules.instruction: Require a complete, source-backed exam roster before editing. Preserve the workbook headers verbatim; include only courses that are not ended, require attendance, and do not explicitly have no final. Normalize only the requested course-code and course-name suffix, use TBD only for genuinely unreleased fields, and sort included rows by normalized exam start time with TBD items handled explicitly. Stage the row manifest and exclusion/unresolved list, then write the workbook and read it back to verify headers, row values, uniqueness, ordering, normalization, and exact coverage against the approved roster before reporting completion.
rules.trigger_description: When a planner must turn a source-reconciled set of remaining required exams into a preformatted spreadsheet artifact without changing its schema or introducing unsupported rows.
required_evidence: Planner/context analyst roster with stable course identifiers and explicit inclusion evidence
Verbatim original headers and confirmation they are unchanged
Per-row provenance for exam timing, attendance requirement, and any TBD field
Explicit excluded or unresolved courses with reasons
Readback evidence for headers, values, normalized names, uniqueness, chronological ordering, and expected-versus-actual row coverage
rules.verification: Independently compare the workbook readback with the approved roster and exclusion list; confirm every included course is covered exactly once, no excluded course appears, headers are byte-for-byte unchanged, suffix normalization is limited to the requested transformation, and rows are ordered by exam start time. Treat unsupported or ambiguous rows as unresolved rather than silently including them.
rules.fallback: If the approved roster, source evidence, headers, or timing is incomplete, pause the write or leave affected fields/records explicitly unresolved; do not infer attendance, exam dates, proctors, or course identity. If the workbook interface or readback is unavailable, report the limitation instead of claiming a verified artifact.

rules.instruction: Independently recompute the exam roster from the authoritative course sources and inspect the preformatted workbook before and after editing. Classify every reviewed course by ended status, attendance requirement, explicit no-final status, and release state; approve only courses that are not ended, must be attended, and are not explicitly no-final. Verify each approved row's source-backed exam fields, genuine TBD usage, requested suffix normalization, unchanged headers, uniqueness, and chronological ordering, then reconcile the workbook one-for-one against the approved set and the explicit exclusion/unresolved list. Do not treat a completed artifact or an implementation manifest as proof of source correctness.
rules.trigger_description: When a spreadsheet must contain a complete, source-backed roster of remaining required final exams compiled from course announcements or email as of a stated cutoff date.
required_evidence: Complete search basis and authority for Canvas/email sources as of the cutoff date
Stable identifier and explicit inclusion or exclusion evidence for every reviewed course
Per-field provenance for every approved exam row and justification for each TBD
Verbatim header comparison and workbook readback evidence
Independent expected-versus-actual row reconciliation, including duplicate, omission, and ordering checks
rules.verification: Recompute the full reviewed-course population independently, compare each workbook row to the approved source-backed roster, confirm excluded or unresolved courses are absent, verify suffix removal is limited to the requested transformation, and confirm rows sort by actual exam start time while TBD placement is explicitly documented.
rules.fallback: If source access, course identity, attendance status, exam release state, workbook readback, or a field comparison is incomplete, report the affected records and evidence gaps and approve only confidently supported rows; do not infer exam attendance, dates, proctors, or missing values.
rules.context_notes: Retain the active exam source-reconciliation and spreadsheet-execution rules; this is a separate verifier-facing contract rather than a replacement for them.

rules.instruction: Review all authoritative Canvas announcements and logged-in email relevant as of the user-specified cutoff date, and produce a complete, source-backed exam roster for downstream spreadsheet entry. Reconcile courses by stable course identifiers, preserve the original table headers as metadata, and for every course classify: not yet ended versus ended, final exam required attendance versus optional/not required, explicitly no final exam, and exam details released versus unresolved. Exclude ended courses, exams the student need not attend, and courses explicitly stating no final exam. For included exams, extract exact course code/name with the requested suffix normalization, start date/time, end date/time or duration if available, location or link, and proctor; default proctor to the instructor only when no different proctor is stated. Mark genuinely unreleased fields TBD, retain provenance and uncertainty per field, and sort only after reconciliation by exam start time.
rules.trigger_description: When a task requires compiling a student's remaining required final exams from Canvas, email, or similar course sources into a preformatted schedule as of a stated date.
required_evidence: Complete search basis for relevant Canvas announcements, email, and workspace context as of the specified cutoff date
Stable course identifier and source evidence for every reviewed course
Explicit evidence for each inclusion or exclusion: course ended status, attendance requirement, final-exam/no-final status, or unresolved release state
Exact source-backed exam fields and per-field provenance for every included course, including the basis for any TBD
Original table headers captured verbatim and confirmed unchanged
Reconciled counts of reviewed, included, excluded, and unresolved courses
Chronological ordering check based on normalized exam start times
rules.verification: Independently compare the reported roster against the complete source search; verify every course is classified exactly once, exclusions satisfy the user's ended/not-required/explicit-no-final criteria, included rows have source-backed attendance and exam evidence, TBD cells reflect genuine missing release information, normalized names and preserved headers match the requested transformation, and included rows are sorted by exam start time.
rules.fallback: If a source, course status, attendance requirement, or exam detail cannot be verified, keep the record in an explicit unresolved list with evidence gaps rather than guessing; provide only confidently included exams for downstream entry and state what confirmation is needed.
rules.context_notes: The only recorded handoff asked the context analyst to inventory Canvas/email sources and determine exam inclusion/exclusion, but no existing rule was used and the evaluation failed despite a completed artifact. This supports adding an exam-specific evidence contract, without asserting that the failure was caused by the downstream file operation or by an API/provider issue.

rules.instruction: Independently inspect the authoritative source records and the current calendar or action state before mutation. Recompute the intended set using stable source identifiers, classify each candidate by the actual requested action, and require explicit evidence that a calendar item is a meeting with a scheduled start—not merely a deadline, submission date, or similarly named record. Validate title, date/time, timezone, location or link, requested reminder offset, and any other action-specific fields against the source. Identify pre-existing actions and duplicates, and provide an explicit excluded/unresolved list for ambiguous or deadline-only candidates. Do not approve mutation when the source supports only deadlines, timing is ambiguous, or the intended action cannot be reproduced. After execution, inspect authoritative provider readback and action logs where available, compare them one-for-one with the independently derived approved set, and report omissions, extras, duplicates, failures, and any unavailable checks.
rules.trigger_description: When an irreversible external action is planned from email, workspace, or calendar sources and an independent verifier must validate the intended target set, distinguish actionable meetings or requests from deadlines and other non-actionable dates, and confirm both pre-action safety and post-action completeness.
required_evidence: Authoritative source descriptions and complete search basis
Per-candidate classification evidence distinguishing meetings from deadlines or other dates
Exact source-backed timing, timezone, title, reminder offset, and required fields for every approved action
Explicit pre-existing, excluded, and unresolved records with reasons
Independent comparison of approved actions with provider readback or authoritative logs, including duplicate, omission, extra, and failure checks
rules.verification: Independent verifier must establish that the requested objects are meetings with explicit start times and that reminders correspond to the user's requested timing; deadline-derived events are not acceptable substitutes.
rules.fallback: If source access, classification evidence, timing, timezone, requested reminder, or readback is incomplete, return the affected records and evidence gaps to the planner and approve only confidently supported actions. If no candidate is explicitly supported as the requested meeting or action, recommend no mutation rather than converting deadlines or inferred dates into calendar events.
rules.context_notes: The trace shows the verifier was asked to inspect emails and the calendar, but the recorded handoff did not reference an active rule. Future use should make the verifier's approval contingent on a reproducible approved set and explicit meeting-versus-deadline evidence before any calendar mutation.

version_history.instruction: Before external actions proceed, independently inspect the authoritative structured and message sources, recompute the in-scope population and missing-item set using stable identifiers, and validate each expected individualized action payload. Confirm the readback strategy and compare eventual execution results against the independently derived expectation, including exclusions, duplicates, omissions, and provider confirmation.
version_history.trigger_description: When a planner needs an independent verifier to validate source reconciliation, expected individualized external actions, and post-action completeness before accepting an irreversible participant-level operation.
required_evidence: Descriptions of each authoritative source checked and the basis for authority
Reconciled counts for total, excluded, matched, and missing in-scope records
Stable identifier, name, contact, and missingness evidence for every expected recipient
Validation that each expected payload contains the required source-backed individualized fields
Provider/readback confirmation and an independent comparison of expected versus completed actions
Explicit duplicate, omission, and exclusion-status checks
version_history.verification: Recompute the expected recipient set independently rather than relying only on the upstream list; compare it with the executed set and provider readback; verify identifiers, individualized content, exclusions, counts, duplicates, omissions, and any unresolved uncertainty.
version_history.fallback: If source systems disagree, expected records cannot be reproduced, or readback is unavailable, return the disputed records and evidence gaps to the planner and do not approve irreversible actions. If verification is incomplete, state exactly which checks remain unresolved rather than treating execution as verified.
version_history.context_notes: The task trace included a direct planner-to-verifier handoff for independent source inspection, computation of the expected in-scope recipient set, individualized payload checks, and authoritative readback validation. Execution then passed with complete coverage, no duplicates or omissions, and independent verification. This adds a verifier-specific contract without changing the successful reconciliation or execution contracts.
version_history.reason: The rule remains supported by the successful execution and should be retained, but the handoff trace explicitly requested post-send inspection of the sent folder for subject, recipients, and body IDs, while the existing contract did not name that artifact-level check. Refining it makes the verifier's post-action evidence requirements more explicit without removing prior guidance.

version_history.instruction: Independently inspect the authoritative structured and message sources, recompute the in-scope population and missing-item set using stable identifiers, and validate each expected individualized action payload before execution. After execution, inspect the system's authoritative sent-message or action log when available, confirming subject, recipient, and required source-backed identifiers in each payload; compare that evidence with provider/readback results and the independently derived expected set, including exclusions, duplicates, omissions, and failures.
version_history.trigger_description: When a planner needs an independent verifier to validate source reconciliation, expected individualized external actions, and post-action completeness before accepting an irreversible participant-level operation.
required_evidence: Descriptions of each authoritative source checked and the basis for authority
Reconciled counts for total, excluded, matched, and missing in-scope records
Stable identifier, name, contact, and missingness evidence for every expected recipient
Validation that each expected payload contains the required source-backed individualized fields
Sent-message or authoritative action-log evidence, where available, confirming subject, recipients, and required identifiers
Provider/readback confirmation and an independent comparison of expected versus completed actions
Explicit duplicate, omission, and exclusion-status checks
version_history.verification: Recompute the expected recipient set independently rather than relying only on the upstream list; compare it with both execution readback and the authoritative sent-message/action log; verify identifiers, individualized content, required subject or action fields, exclusions, counts, duplicates, omissions, and any unresolved uncertainty.
version_history.fallback: If source systems disagree, expected records cannot be reproduced, required message fields cannot be inspected, or readback is unavailable, return the disputed records and evidence gaps to the planner and do not approve irreversible actions. If a sent log is unavailable but another authoritative provider record exists, document that limitation and use the available record without claiming the unavailable check was performed.
version_history.context_notes: Retains the existing independent source reconciliation, pre-action payload validation, readback, and completeness checks. Adds the successful trace's explicit post-send inspection of the sent folder for subject, recipients, and body identifiers, generalized to an authoritative sent-message or action log. No unsupported failure or task-specific detail is introduced.
version_history.reason: The current task failed despite creating and verifying many events: the execution used camera-ready deadlines as if they were meetings and scheduled reminders from those deadlines. The existing verifier rule's successful historical guidance on independent reconciliation and readback remains useful, but its trigger and payload were too focused on participant-level submissions and did not force explicit pre-mutation classification of calendar candidates. This refinement adds that missing calendar-specific safety check while retaining independent source inspection, stable identifiers, pre-existing-action handling, post-action readback, and completeness reconciliation. The failure is tied to an unsafe handoff outcome, not an API/provider failure.

rules.instruction: Review the available native interface contract and workspace conventions, then translate the planner-approved multi-item action set into a complete, machine-checkable artifact package for execution and verification. Preserve stable source identifiers, per-item timing and timezone, reminder settings, descriptions, provenance, exclusions, and uncertainty. Define validation checks that reconcile the manifest, native contract, execution outcomes, and provider readback one-for-one, including counts, duplicates, omissions, extras, and partial-completion status. Do not add unsupported items or treat a structurally valid artifact as proof that the external action succeeded.
rules.trigger_description: When a planner has an approved multi-item external-action set and an integrator must prepare or review the native interface contract, execution manifest, and verification package before and after implementation.
required_evidence: Upstream approved item set with stable identifiers and explicit exclusions or unresolved items
Native interface requirements and relevant workspace conventions
Per-item source-backed fields, provenance, and uncertainty
A manifest whose expected count reconciles with the approved set
A verification checklist covering provider readback, field correctness, duplicates, omissions, extras, and partial completion
rules.verification: Check that the native contract accepts every approved item without introducing unsupported fields or records; verify manifest counts and identifiers against the approved set; require provider readback for each item and reconcile pre-existing, newly successful, failed, and remaining items one-for-one. Keep completion unconfirmed whenever any approved item lacks verified external coverage.
rules.fallback: If the native interface, workspace instructions, or upstream approved set is incomplete, return the specific schema or evidence gaps and do not certify the artifact as ready; preserve unresolved items and require downstream readback before completion is reported.
rules.context_notes: The trace contains a planner-to-integrator request to review the native contract and workspace structure, and the successful outcome included a ready native contract, manifest, and verification report for a multi-item calendar action. This complements—not replaces—the existing context-analysis and implementation rules by defining the integrator's artifact and cross-check responsibilities.

rules.instruction: Inspect the complete relevant mailbox, workspace materials, and existing calendar context before any calendar mutation. Identify every candidate meeting item, distinguish actual meetings from deadlines or other dates, and extract the authoritative title, date, time, timezone, location or link, and the exact requested reminder timing. Reconcile duplicates and conflicting updates using message/source chronology and explicit authority; preserve each item's provenance and uncertainty. Return a complete calendar-ready set, including excluded or unresolved candidates and why, so downstream execution schedules reminders for the intended meetings rather than inferring events from unrelated deadlines.
rules.trigger_description: When a request requires finding one or more meetings or meeting-related items across email and workspace sources and translating explicit reminder requests into calendar-ready specifications.
required_evidence: Search basis demonstrating coverage of relevant email and workspace sources
Source evidence that each included item is a meeting rather than a deadline or unrelated date
Exact date, time, timezone, title, and reminder request for every included item
Provenance and conflict-resolution evidence for updated or duplicate items
Reconciled counts plus an explicit list of excluded and unresolved candidates
rules.verification: Independently compare the returned items with the authoritative source records, check timezone and reminder-offset interpretation, verify that every requested meeting is represented exactly once, and confirm that deadlines or ambiguous items are not silently converted into meeting reminders.
rules.fallback: If a source is inaccessible, timing or timezone is ambiguous, or competing updates cannot be resolved, report the affected item and evidence gap without guessing; provide only confidently supported calendar specifications and state what confirmation is required before scheduling.

rules.instruction: After execution of a multi-part shop action, perform a final integrity audit across the approved product manifest, sorted CSV attachment, category readback, subscriber manifest, and delivery evidence. Reconcile category assignments and subscriber deliveries separately and one-for-one, distinguish pre-existing, newly successful, failed, duplicate, omitted, extra, and unverifiable records, and verify the literal category name, CSV schema/order/content, attachment identity, recipient mapping, and rendered template. Return an explicit open completion gate and resumable remainder whenever either action set is incomplete; never convert aggregate or partial evidence into completion.
rules.trigger_description: When a shop workflow has mutated product categorization and sent a shared artifact-backed notification, and an integrator must perform the final cross-artifact completeness and integrity audit before completion is reported.
required_evidence: Planner-approved product and subscriber manifests with stable identifiers and exclusions
Readback or authoritative logs for category assignments using pagination-complete retrieval
CSV headers, ordering, row content, attachment identity, and literal category-name checks
Recipient-level delivery evidence mapped to each approved subscriber; aggregate/BCC evidence explicitly labeled insufficient
Separate counts and duplicate, omission, extra, failure, and remaining-record checks for category and email actions
rules.verification: Compare approved manifests with artifact contents, category-provider readback, and delivery evidence independently and jointly; verify one-to-one identity and counts, exact category naming, CSV conformance and sorting, recipient mapping, template/attachment consistency, and that no unresolved remainder is hidden by aggregate evidence.
rules.fallback: If any source manifest, artifact, provider readback, delivery log, or count is unavailable, report confirmed versus unverified coverage separately, preserve the exact product/subscriber remainder, and do not certify completion. Treat aggregate email evidence as insufficient for recipient-level confirmation.
rules.context_notes: The trace included a planner-to-integrator request for a final integrity audit after mutations, while execution evidence showed partial category readback and incomplete, duplicate-prone aggregate email evidence. This contract adds the missing integrator-facing reconciliation role; it does not treat provider pagination/API inconsistency as a protocol failure.

rules.instruction: Require a complete approved product and subscriber manifest before mutation, including stable product IDs, the literal category name, sorted CSV rows, validated template-conformant payloads, and explicit prior-state evidence. Validate the native category and email interfaces, CSV headers/format, attachment contents, and idempotency strategy before sending or assigning. Execute category assignments and subscriber emails in bounded resumable batches with durable per-record checkpoints. After each batch, read back category membership using pagination-complete queries and record product-level outcomes; send emails as individually auditable recipient actions rather than relying on an aggregate BCC as proof. Reconcile category and delivery results separately and one-for-one against the approved sets, keeping completion closed for any unverified, duplicate, omitted, or remaining record.
rules.trigger_description: When a shop workflow must assign a reconciled set of products to a named category and send a CSV-backed individualized email to each subscriber, requiring resumable execution and separate completeness verification for both mutations.
required_evidence: Complete upstream-approved product and subscriber sets with stable identifiers and explicit exclusions or unresolved records
Validated literal category name, sorted CSV schema/rows, attachment content, and rendered email template
Native interface and idempotency validation before mutation
Per-record category and email checkpoints distinguishing prior, newly successful, failed, and unverifiable outcomes
Pagination-complete category readback and recipient-level delivery evidence
Separate one-to-one reconciliation of expected versus completed category assignments and email deliveries, including duplicates, omissions, extras, and remaining records
rules.verification: Compare pre-existing plus newly successful category assignments and deliveries separately with the approved product and subscriber manifests. Verify product identity, exact category name, sorted CSV and attachment conformance, recipient and rendered template content, pagination-complete readback, duplicate/omission/extra checks, and exact remaining work; approve completion only when both sets have one-to-one verified coverage.
rules.fallback: If the manifest, native contract, artifact validation, per-recipient delivery evidence, or pagination-complete readback is unavailable, keep the completion gate closed, preserve confirmed actions, and report exact unresolved product/subscriber IDs with a resumable continuation plan rather than claiming success.
rules.context_notes: The trace used a planner-to-implementer request to prepare the CSV and execution artifacts, but the subsequent run left 28 of 120 category assignments unverified and used aggregate email delivery that did not establish complete recipient-level coverage and showed duplicates. The contract adds execution-stage safeguards for this combined category-and-notification pattern while treating pagination/API inconsistency as an evidence gap requiring reconciliation, not as a protocol prohibition.

rules.instruction: Independently recompute the complete approved product set from authoritative stock-in history and the exact preceding 30-day sales window, applying stock age >90 days and sales <10. Verify ordering by stock-in time ascending and discount ratio ascending for ties, literal category-name fidelity, and CSV schema/content. Separately inspect pagination-complete category readback and recipient-level email delivery evidence, reconciling pre-existing plus newly completed actions one-for-one against the approved product and subscriber manifests. Treat aggregate/BCC messages as insufficient for individual coverage, identify duplicates, omissions, extras, and unresolved records, and approve completion only when both category and email sets are fully evidenced.
rules.trigger_description: When a shop workflow selects products by inventory age and recent sales, assigns them to a named category, and sends a shared CSV-backed notification to subscribers, requiring independent post-action completeness verification.
required_evidence: Authoritative stock-in and sales sources with complete product-population search basis and exact time-window boundaries
Per-product evidence for both strict predicates, stable IDs, discount ratios, and ordering keys
Independent CSV header/format/content and literal category-name checks
Pagination-complete category readback distinguishing pre-existing, newly successful, missing, duplicate, and extra assignments
Recipient-level delivery evidence mapped one-to-one to every approved subscriber, with aggregate-only evidence explicitly marked insufficient
Separate product and subscriber counts, remaining IDs, and duplicate/omission/extra checks
rules.verification: Recompute eligibility and sorting independently; compare the approved product and subscriber manifests separately with artifact, category-provider, and delivery readback. Verify exact category naming, CSV conformance, pagination completeness, recipient identity, and individualized delivery evidence. Approval requires one-to-one coverage with no unresolved remainder, duplicates, omissions, or extras in either action set.
rules.fallback: If complete product history, sales-window evidence, paginated category readback, or recipient-level delivery logs are unavailable, report confirmed and unverified coverage separately, preserve the exact product/subscriber remainder, and keep approval closed. Do not infer that an aggregate message proves delivery to every subscriber.
rules.context_notes: The current trace routed a generic planner request to the verifier, while execution produced only partial category readback because of pagination/API inconsistency and aggregate email evidence with duplicate/incomplete recipient coverage. The existing context-analysis and implementation rules cover preparation and execution, but no clearance-specific verifier contract exists. This rule adds independent post-action reconciliation without treating the provider inconsistency as a protocol prohibition.

rules.instruction: Inspect authoritative product, stock-history, and recent-sales sources plus workspace template/schema, subscriber data, and the native contract before mutation. Reconcile products by stable product ID and prove both strict predicates independently: stock-in time older than 90 days (using stock-in history, not an unsubstantiated proxy such as creation date) and fewer than 10 units sold in the exact preceding 30-day window. Produce the complete approved product manifest sorted by stock-in time ascending, then discount ratio ascending for ties, preserving the literal category name. Validate CSV headers, row shape, discount calculation, attachment identity, and rendered template. Reconcile subscriber IDs and recipient addresses across all authoritative sources; if counts or target populations disagree, record the competing evidence and leave the recipient manifest unresolved rather than selecting a contract/evaluator target by assumption. Include prior category/delivery state when available and explicit excluded/unresolved records for every gap.
rules.trigger_description: When a shop workflow must identify products using strict inventory-age and recent-sales predicates, assign them to an exactly named category, and prepare a sorted CSV-backed notification set for subscribers whose target population may be defined across multiple workspace or contract sources.
required_evidence: Complete authoritative product population and stable product IDs
Per-included-product evidence for stock-in timestamp older than 90 days and sales strictly below 10 in the exact preceding 30-day interval
Discount ratios and explicit ordering keys supporting tie handling
Workspace evidence for literal category name, CSV headers/format, template, attachment name, and native contract
Subscriber source records with stable IDs, recipient mapping, declared counts, and evidence reconciling every source
Explicit competing-evidence report for any count, recipient, predicate, or date-boundary conflict
Prior category assignment and delivery state where available
Reconciled product and subscriber counts with duplicate/omission checks
rules.verification: Independently recompute product eligibility from stock-in history and the exact sales window, verify sorting and CSV/template conformance, and reconcile subscriber IDs, recipients, and counts across authoritative sources. Any unresolved source conflict, unsupported date proxy, duplicate, omission, or recipient-target mismatch keeps the manifest unresolved and blocks downstream mutation.
rules.fallback: If subscriber counts, recipient identity, stock-in age, sales-window boundaries, or native-contract targets conflict, do not choose a value or begin category/email mutations. Return competing evidence, a conservative confirmed set, and the exact confirmation needed; keep the manifest and completion gate closed until the conflict is resolved.
rules.context_notes: Retains the prior rule's general preparation contract and strengthens it based on the observed unresolved 90-versus-96 recipient discrepancy and the need to distinguish the requested stock-in-age predicate from a merely available creation-date filter.

version_history.instruction: Inspect authoritative product, stock-history, and recent-sales records plus workspace template/schema and subscriber data before any mutation. Reconcile the complete product population by stable product ID, include only products stocked for more than 90 days and sold fewer than 10 units in the preceding 30 days, and preserve evidence for both predicates. Sort the approved products by stock-in time ascending, then discount ratio ascending for ties. Capture the exact category name, including punctuation, and produce a recipient-level subscriber manifest rather than relying on a single BCC aggregate. Validate the CSV headers, row format, attachment contents, and per-recipient rendered email payload; identify pre-existing category assignments or prior deliveries when available, and separate excluded or unresolved products and subscribers without guessing.
version_history.trigger_description: When a shop workflow must identify products using combined inventory-age and recent-sales criteria, assign them to a named category, and prepare a sorted CSV-backed notification set for subscribers.
required_evidence: Complete authoritative product-population search and stable product IDs
Independent evidence for stock-in age greater than 90 days and fewer than 10 sales in the specified 30-day window for every included product
Exact stock-in timestamps and discount ratios supporting the required ordering, including tie handling
Workspace evidence for the literal category name, CSV headers/format, email template, and attachment naming
Subscriber source and one-to-one subscriber ID to recipient mapping, with duplicate or invalid addresses identified
Evidence of existing category assignments or prior notification state where available
Reconciled included, excluded, and unresolved counts with duplicate and omission checks
version_history.verification: Independent recomputation and one-to-one manifest checks must precede mutation; later execution should separately read back category assignments and each subscriber delivery, preserving an explicit remainder if either set is incomplete.
version_history.fallback: If stock history, sales-window boundaries, product identity, CSV schema, template, category name, subscriber mapping, or prior-action state is incomplete or conflicting, keep affected records unresolved and do not infer values. Provide only confidently supported products and recipients, state the exact evidence gaps, and leave downstream mutations gated on a complete machine-checkable manifest and later provider readback.
version_history.context_notes: The task's only recorded handoff was a concise inventory/context inspection request, while execution later attempted 120 category assignments but verified only 92 because 28 remained affected by pagination/API inconsistency; notification evidence used two aggregate messages and did not establish complete recipient-level coverage, with duplicates visible. This new preparation contract strengthens expected-set reconciliation, exact CSV/template requirements, and per-recipient accounting without treating the provider inconsistency as a collaboration failure.
version_history.reason: Refine the existing woocommerce_clearance_product_subscriber_manifest rule. Retain its evidence-first product selection, stable IDs, literal category name, sorted CSV, template validation, prior-state capture, and explicit unresolved records. Add a mandatory distinction between stock-in history and creation date, require exact 30-day window evidence, and add a hard pre-mutation reconciliation step for conflicting subscriber counts/targets. The current trace specifically reported 90 versus 96 recipients as unresolved while still presenting an actionable 120-product set, and the evaluation failed; these additions address that handoff omission rather than an external-system failure.

rules.instruction: Require a complete source-backed customer manifest and a finalized native contract before any mutation, including stable customer IDs, typed CRM payloads, rendered template-conformant email payloads, prior-completion state, and an idempotency key. Validate the contract and payloads before a canary; treat a canary as validation only, never as completion. Execute the full approved set in bounded resumable batches, checkpointing each CRM and email outcome separately and reading back provider state after batches. Preserve successful work, report attempted/successful/failed/remaining records exactly, and keep completion closed until CRM and email coverage each reconcile one-for-one with the approved population. Do not coerce malformed status values into sent or synced; flag them as unverifiable and require explicit readback or a safe continuation plan.
rules.trigger_description: When a reconciled customer population requires paired CRM synchronization and individualized email delivery, with external mutations that must be completed and verified per customer.
required_evidence: Complete approved customer manifest with stable IDs and explicit exclusions or unresolved records
Finalized native contract and schema/type validation before mutation
Per-customer CRM and email payloads with source provenance and template conformance
Evidence distinguishing prior, newly successful, failed, and unverifiable CRM/email actions
Durable batch checkpoints and provider readback sufficient for idempotent resumption
Independent one-to-one reconciliation of expected versus CRM-completed and email-completed records, including duplicates, omissions, extras, and remaining work
rules.verification: Independently compare the union of prior and newly successful CRM records and emails against the approved customer set; verify typed status values, recipients, rendered template content, stable identifiers, checkpoint/readback consistency, and separate CRM/email coverage. Any malformed status, missing artifact, unavailable readback, or nonzero remainder keeps completion unapproved.
rules.fallback: If the manifest, credentials/interface contract, payload types, template rendering, or readback is incomplete, pause affected mutations and return the evidence gaps. If execution is partial, preserve successful records and provide exact CRM and email continuation sets without resending confirmed successes; if status values are malformed, leave them unverifiable rather than guessing.
rules.context_notes: This run stopped after one canary email, leaving 90 required emails missing; CRM rows existed but their sent-status values were malformed, the native contract remained draft, and the verification report was absent. The contract addresses those handoff-relevant execution and accounting gaps without attributing them to an external provider failure.

rules.instruction: Independently recompute the eligible customers from authoritative completed-order records for the requested time window, then verify CRM synchronization and welcome-email delivery separately for every customer. Read back CRM rows and delivery evidence, validate stable customer identity, source-backed fields, typed sync/email status, recipient, and template rendering, and reconcile pre-existing plus newly completed actions one-for-one against the approved set. Treat a canary as validation only; any missing, malformed, unverifiable, duplicate, or extra record keeps completion unapproved and must be reported with a resumable remainder.
rules.trigger_description: When customers selected from a completed-order time-window rule require both CRM synchronization and individualized welcome-email delivery, and an independent verifier must confirm source eligibility and complete post-action coverage.
required_evidence: Independent complete order-window search and per-customer eligibility counts
Stable customer IDs and source-backed identity mapping
CRM readback proving synchronized fields and valid typed status values for each eligible customer
Email delivery evidence for each recipient, including rendered template conformance
Separate CRM and email counts reconciled against the approved population
Explicit duplicate, omission, extra, malformed, unverifiable, and remaining-record checks
A closed completion decision whenever either CRM or email coverage is incomplete
rules.verification: Recompute eligibility independently; compare CRM and email completion sets separately and jointly with the approved customer set; inspect provider readback or authoritative delivery logs, validate fields, types, recipients, and template content, and approve only when both action sets have exact one-to-one coverage with no unresolved records.
rules.fallback: If source access, CRM readback, email delivery evidence, or typed status fields are unavailable, report confirmed CRM and email coverage separately, preserve malformed or ambiguous states as unverifiable, list exact customer IDs needing continuation, and keep approval closed.
rules.context_notes: The trace used a generic planner-to-verifier request and verification was blocked: only one canary email was sent, 90 required emails were missing, CRM sent-status values were malformed, and no verification report existed. This adds the missing verifier-facing contract; it does not treat those issues as an API failure.

rules.instruction: Independently recompute the complete low-stock population from the authoritative inventory using stock_quantity < stock_threshold, reconcile stable product IDs and counts, and inspect both spreadsheet readback and notification evidence. Compare pre-existing plus newly completed records one-for-one with the approved set; validate each row's product identity and source values, each notification's recipient and individualized template content, and detect duplicates, omissions, extras, and failures. Treat any remaining approved record as an open blocker and do not approve completion until both artifact and notification coverage are complete, or explicitly report the exact resumable remainder.
rules.trigger_description: When inventory records below a strict source-defined threshold have been written to a spreadsheet and paired with individualized notifications, and an independent verifier must confirm completeness and correctness after external actions.
required_evidence: Authoritative inventory search basis and independent strict-inequality recomputation
Stable product IDs, quantities, thresholds, and reconciled population counts
Spreadsheet identity, schema, provider readback, and per-product row coverage
Per-notification recipient, individualized product content, template conformance, and provider/readback evidence
Explicit duplicate, omission, extra, failure, and remaining-record checks
rules.verification: Recompute the expected set independently, compare it separately against sheet rows and notifications, then verify the intersection and union are consistent with the approved products. Any nonzero remainder, unverifiable provider state, or mismatch keeps completion unapproved.
rules.fallback: If inventory, sheet, or notification evidence is incomplete, report only confirmed coverage, list affected product IDs and evidence gaps, and return a continuation set based on durable readback rather than treating partial execution as complete.
rules.context_notes: The run identified a complete low-stock set but only partially populated the sheet and sent notifications; the planner's verifier handoff was generic and did not reference an active inventory-specific verification contract. This adds a verifier-facing contract for independent recomputation and honest partial-completion accounting without attributing the failure to an API/provider fault.
