rules.instruction: Before any mutation, inspect the authoritative product inventory and workspace instructions, then produce a complete low-stock manifest using the strict predicate stock_quantity < stock_threshold. Preserve stable product IDs and source values, exclude products that do not satisfy the predicate, and reconcile the full product population so omissions and duplicates are visible. Also extract the exact purchasing recipient, email-template requirements, sheet identity/tab/headers, and any idempotency or existing-record evidence needed by the implementer. Do not send emails or write the sheet; return approved records, excluded records, and unresolved items with provenance.
rules.trigger_description: When a workflow must identify all inventory records below a source-defined safety threshold and prepare a spreadsheet-and-notification action set before external mutations.
required_evidence: Authoritative inventory source and complete product-population search basis
Per-product ID, name, stock quantity, threshold, and explicit strict-inequality evidence for every low-stock record
Reconciled counts covering reviewed, included, excluded, and unresolved products, with duplicate/omission checks
Exact recipient address and template placeholder/content requirements from workspace sources
Sheet identity, tab, headers, and evidence for any existing records or prior notifications
Explicit provenance and uncertainty for every unresolved or conflicting record
rules.verification: Independently recompute stock_quantity < stock_threshold for the full authoritative product population; verify stable IDs, counts, exclusions, duplicate/omission status, template and recipient extraction, and sheet metadata against the original sources. Confirm that the manifest is sufficient for one-to-one downstream reconciliation.
rules.fallback: If WooCommerce, workspace files, the sheet schema, recipient, or template cannot be verified, return the affected records and evidence gaps; do not guess thresholds, contacts, placeholders, or sheet columns. Provide only confirmed low-stock products and mark the rest unresolved.
rules.context_notes: The observed handoff asked for inventory inspection and operational details but did not specify a structured, completeness-checkable payload. The run did successfully identify 110 low-stock products and the recipient/template/sheet context, while execution later remained partial (30 of 110 sheet rows and 5 of 110 notifications), so this contract strengthens upstream reconciliation and makes the downstream expected set explicit without attributing the failure to an API/provider issue.

rules.instruction: Inspect the authoritative order and customer sources, CRM schema/current state, email template, and available delivery configuration without mutating them. Reconcile orders in the requested time window by stable customer identifiers, count completed orders per customer, and produce the complete eligible population exactly once. For every eligible customer, provide source-backed identity/contact fields, the exact CRM field mapping and typed values, email recipient and rendered template payload, and evidence of any already-synced or already-emailed state. Separate confirmed, already-completed, excluded, and unresolved records; do not treat a canary or malformed status representation as completion. Require a machine-checkable native contract and manifest suitable for downstream execution and readback.
rules.trigger_description: When a workflow must identify customers with exactly one completed order within a recent time window and prepare a synchronized CRM update plus individualized welcome-email action set before any external mutation.
required_evidence: Complete order search basis and authoritative customer/order sources
Stable customer identifiers and per-customer completed-order count evidence
Exact source-backed CRM fields with schema-compatible types
Per-recipient template-conformant email payload and recipient evidence
Evidence distinguishing prior CRM sync and email completion from pending work

If Google Finance semantics or historical coverage cannot be established, report a conditional result and the precise limitation instead of selecting the earliest-looking year.

rules.context_notes: The task succeeded, and the researcher-to-planner trace supplied a reproducible dated path, revision identifiers, transition evidence, click convention, and a direct-link check. rules.instruction: Independently enumerate the relevant 2012 Scientific Reports conference-proceedings articles, verify each candidate's collection membership and publication date, and inspect reproducible full text or indexed text for every exclusion-term variant (plasmons, plasmonics, plasmon, and plasmonic). For the uniquely qualifying article, identify the nano-compound from a direct passage, preserve the article citation and evidence trail, and remove any requested prefix only after confirming the compound's identity. Report inaccessible candidates, ambiguous absence claims, and competing interpretations explicitly rather than accepting a bare candidate answer.
rules.trigger_description: When a verifier independently checks which article in a specified year's scientific journal conference proceedings is uniquely selected by the absence of technical terms and must identify the compound studied in that article.
required_evidence: A reproducible journal or proceedings index establishing the 2012 candidate set and collection scope
Evidence that every considered article belongs to the requested proceedings collection
Full-text or stable indexed-text checks for all relevant spelling variants of the exclusion terms, with inaccessible text distinguished from confirmed absence
A direct quotation or faithful transcription from the selected article identifying the studied compound
Candidate-by-candidate elimination and uniqueness logic
Citation/source links and explicit treatment of ambiguity, redirects, dates, or incomplete access
Final answer normalized only after compound identification, with any requested nano prefix removed at the end
rules.verification: Planner checks the proceedings scope and complete candidate inventory, confirms each exclusion-term occurrence or absence against the cited text, validates the compound against a direct article passage, recomputes the uniqueness logic, and verifies that prefix normalization did not alter the compound identity.
rules.fallback: If the proceedings index, article full text, or historical text is inaccessible, return all strongest candidates with the accessible metadata/snippets, explicitly mark absence and compound claims as uncertain, and do not certify a unique answer from title, abstract, or failed search alone.
rules.context_notes: The actual handoff was planner to verifier, but no rule was attached. The verifier returned the wrong compound (silicon crystals; evaluated answer diamond) without candidate-by-candidate proceedings scope evidence, full-text checks for all exclusion-term variants, or a direct passage identifying the compound. This indicates an evidence and disambiguation gap, not an API/provider failure. The existing researcher-facing rule remains useful and is not replaced.

The exact text identifying the bug fix and named command/API object
Context or adjacent-entry evidence supporting interpretation of relational wording such as 'other'
A stable source link or revision identifier
Explicit uncertainty notes for ambiguous version, terminology, redirects, or incomplete access

rules.fallback: If the exact historical changelog is unavailable, use the closest reproducible release or repository revision and label the limitation; return the strongest supported candidate with the relevant excerpt, or list candidates conditionally when the wording does not uniquely identify one.

rules.instruction: Return an independently reproducible audit of the numerical calculation to the planner. Identify the exact reaction row, report every input with cell/row and unit provenance, transcribe the final equation from the specified translation exactly, and define every symbol so that a listed kinetic constant is not silently substituted for the requested velocity. Show full-precision substitution and intermediate arithmetic, perform a dimensional/unit check and any required conversions, round only the final velocity to four decimal places, and compare plausible parameter or equation interpretations when the source is ambiguous.
rules.trigger_description: When a verifier returns an independently checked numerical result computed from a specified spreadsheet row using an equation from a translated or historical scientific primary source.
required_evidence: Evidence identifying the exact workbook reaction row and every numerical input, with cell/row provenance and units
Faithful transcription of the specified paper translation's final equation and definitions for all symbols
An explicit full-precision substitution and arithmetic trail that a planner can recompute
A dimensional consistency and unit-conversion check
A final result rounded to exactly four decimal places under a stated rounding convention
Evidence distinguishing the requested velocity from catalytic or other listed constants
Explicitly labeled alternative calculations for materially plausible row, parameter, unit, or equation interpretations
Source provenance and limitations for both workbook and translation
rules.verification: Planner re-reads the cited row and translated equation, checks each input and symbol definition, independently recomputes the formula with unrounded values, confirms dimensional consistency and conversions, verifies that the output is velocity rather than a copied input constant, and checks final-only rounding. If alternatives are reported, planner confirms their bases and selects a definitive result only when the source supports one.
rules.fallback: If the workbook row, translated equation, symbol meanings, units, or expected parameter convention cannot be established unambiguously, return conditional calculations for each supported interpretation and identify the decisive missing evidence; do not certify a bare rounded number or assume that a listed rate constant is itself the requested velocity.
rules.context_notes: The only observed return handoff was verifier to planner and was incorrect: it reported 0.0429, effectively the workbook's catalytic-constant value, after applying a stated formula, while evaluation expected 0.0424. The trace supplied no attached rule identifier and did not provide enough source-level evidence to determine whether the discrepancy was an input extraction, equation transcription, parameter convention, or arithmetic issue. This contract fills the missing return-direction evidence protocol without attributing the error to an API/provider failure.

rules.instruction: Inspect the complete attached workbook and the specified NIH translation of the historical paper. Extract every numerical input for the requested reaction row, transcribe the paper's final equation exactly (including parameter definitions, units, and parentheses), and compute the velocity using that equation—not a related or rearranged variant. Show a substitution line with unrounded intermediate values, verify units and the requested rounding to four decimal places, and distinguish values taken directly from the workbook from values inferred or converted from the paper. If multiple row labels, parameter conventions, or equation readings are plausible, report them explicitly and identify which one is best supported.
rules.trigger_description: When a task asks for a numerical scientific quantity from a specified row in an attached spreadsheet using a particular equation from a translated or historical primary source.

rules.verification: Re-read the workbook row and primary-source equation, compare each reported input and symbol definition with the sources, independently recompute the formula using full precision, check dimensional consistency, and verify that only the final value—not intermediate terms—was rounded to four decimal places.
rules.fallback: If exact source values or equation semantics cannot be established, provide clearly labeled conditional calculations and the evidence limitation; do not return a bare rounded number or silently substitute a familiar modern formula.
rules.context_notes: The only recorded handoff was planner to researcher for an attached spreadsheet plus a translated historical scientific paper. The returned value 0.0429 was evaluated incorrect against 0.0424, so the reusable gap is not generic spreadsheet reading but auditable extraction of the specified row and exact final-equation calculation. The trace does not indicate an API/provider failure; it indicates insufficiently documented inputs, equation interpretation, or arithmetic/rounding provenance.

rules.instruction: Independently inspect the complete workbook row and the specified translated historical paper. Show the substitution and intermediate arithmetic, check dimensional consistency, apply rounding only to the final result to four decimal places, and explicitly resolve or report competing parameter, row-label, unit-conversion, or equation interpretations.

A recomputable result rounded to exactly four decimal places under a stated convention

rules.fallback: If the workbook row, translation, or equation cannot be read unambiguously, return conditional calculations for each supported interpretation, identify the unavailable evidence, and do not certify a bare rounded value or substitute a familiar modern equation.
rules.context_notes: The task used a planner-to-verifier handoff without an attached rule and was evaluated incorrect (0.0429 versus 0.0424). The verifier request named the workbook row and equation but did not require a source-backed transcription, cell-level inputs, or a recomputable arithmetic trail. This is a handoff evidence/provenance gap, not evidence of an API or provider failure. The existing planner-to-researcher rule remains useful; this adds its missing verifier-direction companion.

rules.instruction: Inspect the provided template and preserve its headers and file identity. Search all specified authoritative sources as of the stated date, reconcile announcements and email records, and build a candidate matrix for every course. Apply the request's inclusion rules explicitly: retain only still-relevant exams the student must attend, exclude completed, optional, and explicitly exam-free courses, normalize requested course-code/name formatting, mark genuinely unreleased details as TBD, and sort by start time. Return exact proposed rows plus source evidence and an inclusion/exclusion rationale so the implementer can populate the workbook without inference.
rules.trigger_description: When compiling a time-sensitive academic schedule from multiple authenticated institutional sources, with inclusion/exclusion rules, unresolved details, formatting constraints, and a required spreadsheet or tabular deliverable.

source_reconciliation.exam_status: required, optional, no exam, completed, or unresolved

selection_rationale.included: why each row remains required as of cutoff
selection_rationale.excluded: courses excluded and the rule applied

required_evidence: Exact template headers and output constraints confirmed before population
Coverage of every specified authoritative source, including both announcement and email channels
Source-backed status and exam details for every included row
Explicit exclusion rationale for completed, optional, and explicitly exam-free courses
Clear treatment of missing or unreleased details as TBD and default proctor handling
A reconciliation/coverage summary and chronological ordering check
rules.verification: Independently compare the completed table against the preserved template headers, recheck every included and excluded course against the source records and cutoff date, verify normalization, duplicate absence, TBD usage, and chronological start-time ordering. Distinguish source-confirmed facts from inference and ensure the saved workbook remains at the requested identity.
rules.fallback: If an institutional source, message category, or detail is inaccessible, return the verified partial matrix, unresolved courses and fields, and exact follow-up checks; populate only source-supported rows and use TBD where the request permits rather than guessing.
rules.context_notes: This contract is supported by a successful trace in which the analyst was asked to inspect the workbook and authoritative announcement/email sources, and the final deliverable reconciled all source fields and four email notifications with the remaining rows from announcements, preserved exact headers, produced 46 chronological rows, excluded nine exam-free courses, removed suffixes, and matched the reference output. It adds reusable provenance, cutoff, and spreadsheet-integrity requirements without encoding institution-specific details.

rules.instruction: Inspect the provided workbook template and preserve its exact headers and output identity. Search both authenticated announcement and email sources as of the stated cutoff date, reconcile records course by course, and determine only the remaining final exams the student must attend. Exclude completed courses, optional or non-attendance exams, and courses explicitly stating there is no final. Normalize course codes and names by removing the requested suffix, use the instructor as proctor unless another proctor is stated, mark unreleased details as TBD, and return source-backed candidate rows already sorted by exam start time together with inclusion/exclusion rationale and any conflicts or uncertainty.

course_records.attendance_status: required, optional, no exam, completed, or unresolved

Explicit TBD treatment for genuinely unreleased fields and conflicts or uncertainty

rules.fallback: If Canvas announcements or email cannot be fully accessed, return a verified partial course matrix, identify inaccessible sources and unresolved courses/fields, and do not infer required attendance. Mark genuinely unreleased details TBD and state the exact follow-up retrieval needed.
rules.context_notes: The planner-to-researcher handoff in this task was unregistered and brief, yet the overall execution passed with a complete workbook, source reconciliation across announcements and four email notifications, 46 chronological rows, nine explicitly exam-free courses excluded, and no duplicate codes or suffixes. This supports making the researcher contract more explicit while leaving the successful context-analyst contract unchanged; the evidence concerns handoff completeness, not source-access or provider failure.

rules.instruction: Inspect the workbook structure before writing, then populate only the source-supported rows supplied by the research handoff. Preserve the exact existing headers, workbook identity, and required sheet structure; apply requested name/code normalization, use TBD only for genuinely unreleased fields, retain only required remaining attendance items, sort by confirmed exam start time, and avoid duplicates or incidental formatting changes. After saving, reopen and verify headers, row count/content, ordering, normalization, exclusions, and output path.

template.structure_constraints: columns, existing formatting, and file-name requirements

rows.exam_fields: values mapped to unchanged headers, including TBD where justified

Every written row traceable to the researcher's source-backed records and inclusion decision
Proof that excluded completed, optional, and explicitly exam-free items were not written
Chronological start-time ordering and duplicate checks
Verification after save that headers and workbook identity remain unchanged
Clear distinction between confirmed values, TBD values, and any unavailable validation
rules.verification: Reopen the saved workbook independently, compare headers and sheet identity with the template, check each row against the supplied evidence and cutoff-based selection, validate normalized names/codes, detect duplicates, and verify nondecreasing exam start times. Treat successful file creation alone as insufficient; report any source or workbook checks that could not be performed.
rules.fallback: If the research payload is incomplete or the workbook cannot be safely inspected, preserve the original file, report missing rows/fields or access limitations, and populate only unambiguous source-supported data; use TBD only where the source explicitly leaves a detail unreleased and request targeted follow-up for the remainder.
rules.context_notes: The contract deliberately separates research/source eligibility from mechanical workbook population: implementers should not infer attendance or exam details when the research handoff is incomplete.

rules.instruction: Establish an isolated baseline and inspect the complete authoritative LM-client call path before editing. Inventory every standard and Azure construction/request path, including legacy and instance-client branches, model/deployment/engine/request-model mapping, chat-versus-completion selection, credential precedence and provider-auth interaction, endpoint/API-version construction, public configuration surfaces, and cache-key inputs. Implement the smallest backward-compatible change: preserve standard-user cache identities and legacy behavior, pass only arguments accepted by the targeted SDK, treat Azure deployment names as deployment identifiers rather than evidence of model family, and use reliable configuration or explicit capability information for request routing. Add focused regressions for standard and Azure initialization, custom deployment names, conflicting argument combinations, chat and completion dispatch, credential precedence/provider-auth, and unchanged standard cache behavior. Report exact SDK/interpreter versions, baseline diagnosis, source and diff rationale, focused/broader/static results, and unavailable live-service coverage separately.

required_evidence: Isolated baseline reproduction or precise SDK signature/source diagnosis tied to the affected call path
Inventory of all standard/Azure constructors and request dispatch branches, including indirect callers and public configuration surfaces
Explicit mapping and precedence for logical model, deployment/engine, and request-model arguments, with custom Azure deployment coverage
Evidence that chat/completion routing does not rely on deployment-name heuristics and matches actual integration behavior
Credential precedence, provider-auth conflict avoidance, endpoint/API-version evidence, and exact SDK/interpreter versions

Concise diff rationale covering authoritative source and any documentation or example updates
rules.verification: Inspect every cited production path and the complete diff independently. Compare constructor and request arguments with the exact targeted SDK contract, exercise standard and Azure fake/isolated clients with custom deployment names and conflicting model/engine/deployment inputs, verify routing and credential/provider-auth behavior, and compare standard cache keys before and after. Distinguish deterministic fake-client, compile, and generic test evidence from live authentication/backend coverage; do not claim full compatibility when the target SDK or service was unavailable.
rules.fallback: If the target SDK, credentials, or live Azure service cannot be exercised, provide the isolated reproduction, explicit version matrix, source/signature analysis, argument/capability/cache mapping, narrowly scoped patch, and focused fake-client/static checks. List exact remaining runtime checks and preserve uncertainty rather than claiming live initialization, authentication, or complete cache compatibility.
rules.context_notes: Retained the prior rule's baseline-first workflow, complete call-path inspection, credential/endpoint/provider-auth checks, capability validation, minimal backward-compatible change, documentation consistency, and explicit runtime limitations. Added acceptance evidence exposed by the current trace: the planner handoff was only a generic request to inspect and patch, carried no registered rule, and received F2P 0/3 despite fake-client, compilation, 112-test, and diff-check success. The refinement therefore makes logical model versus Azure deployment/request model, custom-name routing, and standard cache identity explicit; it does not treat the evaluation failure as an SDK/provider failure.

Treat successful local or static checks as partial evidence if the live service or target SDK range was unavailable.

version_history.reason: Refine the existing Azure SDK migration implementation contract. It remains directionally correct and historically supported, but the current sparse planner-to-implementer handoff omitted explicit requirements for custom Azure deployment names, capability routing, argument-conflict behavior, and preservation of standard cache identities. The implementation outcome shows these areas are central to acceptance, while the low F2P score indicates that generic patch-and-test guidance did not reliably transfer them. No guidance is retired; the new contract makes the missing evidence and verification obligations actionable.

rules.instruction: Before implementation, inspect the complete authoritative LM-client call path and all production callers, tests, documentation, and examples. Trace credential precedence, endpoint/API-version construction, provider-auth interaction, and cache-key inputs; identify which legacy standard-user cache identities must remain unchanged. Report exact source locations, confirmed versus inferred behavior, a narrowly scoped compatibility recommendation, and a focused regression matrix for standard and Azure paths, custom deployment names, argument-conflict cases, and cache compatibility. Separate static/source evidence from runtime SDK or live-service coverage.

rules.instruction: Resolve each source independently, record the relevant entities and their exact locations, then normalize terminology and compute the intersection. Explicitly apply scope constraints such as excluding bibliographies, distinguish article content from citations, and report the final intersection with concise source-backed reasoning.
rules.trigger_description: When a research question requires identifying entities across multiple papers or web sources and returning only their verified intersection, especially when source wording and exclusions matter.

rules.verification: A verifier should independently check the cited passages, confirm that each reported entity satisfies every source and scope constraint, and ensure no merely cited or bibliographic item was included.
rules.fallback: If a source cannot be accessed or terminology remains ambiguous, return the partial source matrix and unresolved candidates with explicit uncertainty rather than asserting an intersection; request targeted follow-up retrieval.
rules.context_notes: The only observed handoff used this pattern successfully: the planner asked the researcher to identify entities in multiple papers, exclude bibliographies, compare against a later study, and provide exact sources; the resulting answer was correct. Preserve the emphasis on provenance and scope checking while treating this as a reusable positive contract, not a claim about any specific subject.

Identify the repository's established union/type-resolution and async-concurrency patterns, test harness/mocking conventions, and compatibility risks. Separate confirmed source evidence from assumptions, and recommend the smallest implementation plus focused tests that exercise aggregation, ordering, type resolution, validation, and partial provider failure.

Report deterministic parser results separately from credential-dependent live coverage and distinguish unrelated environment failures.

Recommend the smallest compatibility strategy, including dependency bounds if needed, and provide a focused regression matrix covering each affected object family plus broader and static checks. Separate confirmed runtime evidence from source-level inference and unavailable environments.

rules.instruction: Before implementation, inventory every production use of the third-party language-model SDK, including legacy module-level resources, modern client/resource construction, request dispatch, response extraction, streaming, embeddings, configuration, dependency metadata, documentation/examples, and all callers/tests. Identify compatibility risks in authentication/configuration, model selection, exception behavior, request mocking, and dependency bounds. Recommend the smallest backward-compatible migration and a focused regression matrix for legacy and modern clients, non-streaming and streaming responses, embeddings, initialization/configuration, and mocked transport behavior. Separate confirmed runtime/source evidence from inference and unavailable live-service or test-harness coverage.

rules.instruction: Analyze the language semantics and the provided expression to identify the minimal correction, then return only the requested character name or text while explicitly checking that the corrected expression produces the stated output.

rules.instruction: For probability riddles involving sequential random mechanisms, independently model the state transitions and derive the relevant outcome probabilities or an equivalent invariant. rules.instruction: Implement the blockchain repository refactor only after receiving a bounded operation and interface inventory. Account separately for repository code, service signatures, factory/DI wiring, exports, state-machine/observer integrations, and regression probes. Run fake-connector/repository delegation checks, service behavior and boundary cases, factory construction, compilation/import/static residual-connector searches, and final diff review; separate unavailable live-provider/framework/database checks from implementation defects.
